Formula Cities
Numerous factors influence the nature of growth of cities and peripheral areas, not the least of which are the predominant activities of the cities. Based on the weight placed on various activities, cities may be classified as manufacturing, wholesale, transportation, resort-retirement, retail, diversified, mining, university, political or combination cities. 13/ Because different cities and suburbs have varying needs and plans, they grow in different ways.
The strength, of course, of a population-mileage formula is that it simplifies definition of C/Z-T/A boundaries by applying standardized rules of definition applicable to many municipalities.
The major weakness of such a population-mileage formula is that if it is sufficiently restrictive for some municipalities relative to economic considerations, it is excessively restrictive for others.
